summary: Adds email search to the user index, plus update and destroy actions and routes. It also adds a welcome email callback on the User model.

findings.title: Search term interpolated into SQL
findings.description: The index action puts params[:q] straight into the WHERE clause text. Any authenticated caller controls that SQL fragment. Any API token holder can read or change arbitrary database rows, including other users' api_token values. Pass the search term as a bound parameter. Escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.fix: Pass the search term as a bound parameter. Escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Any user can delete any user
findings.description: The change exempts destroy from require_admin on line 2. The destroy action then deletes any User by id with no ownership check. Any authenticated non-admin can delete every account, including admin accounts. Remove destroy from the require_admin exemption list. Alternatively, scope the lookup to the current user.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.description: The model registers send_welcome_email as an after_save callback. That callback fires on updates as well as on creation. Users get a new welcome email each time an admin updates their record through the new update action. Use after_create_commit so the email goes out once, after the insert commits.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.description: The change adds search, update, destroy and an email callback. The repository has no test or spec directory at all. Nothing catches regressions in authorization or callback behaviour on these endpoints. Add request tests for search, update and destroy with admin and non-admin tokens. Add a model test for the welcome email callback.

candidate.message: Found an unscoped `find(...)` with user-controllable input. If the ActiveRecord model being searched against is sensitive, this may lead to Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) behavior and allow users to read arbitrary records. Scope the find to the current user, e.g. `current_user.accounts.find(params[:id])`.

dropped.reason: The require_admin filter still guards update, so only admins reach this lookup. Admins may legitimately edit any user.
